subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should Gateway WebSocket upgrade admission reject forwarded-header contradictions and untrusted-peer protocol mismatches by default, or should all newly rejecting checks remain behind explicitly enabled Gateway security policy?
rationale: This is a network-facing compatibility and security-boundary choice: current main degrades trust for untrusted proxy headers rather than rejecting connections, while the PR adds both a new pre-upgrade enforcement point and permanent configuration surface.

options.title: Keep compatibility defaults
options.body: Gate every new forwarded-header and protocol rejection behind approved explicit options, while preserving current main’s non-local classification by default.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed admission
options.body: Accept default pre-upgrade rejection as a deliberate behavior change, document the affected proxy deployments, and add upgrade and raw-wire proof.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer the new verifier until the Gateway security model has one maintainer-approved policy for upgrade-time proxy headers.

recommendation.title: Keep compatibility defaults
recommendation.body: Gate every new forwarded-header and protocol rejection behind approved explicit options, while preserving current main’s non-local classification by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion specifically asks this person to decide verifier placement and the new Gateway security policy names.
